# Partner API

S2S API for contracted partners. Base URL: `https://gw.olymptrade.com/partner`

## Onboarding

Partner sends the manager: server IPs (single or CIDR) for the whitelist, default country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) used when POST /users/v1 omits `country`. Partner receives: API key, partner identifier (affiliate ID or ref). Verify with GET /ping/v1.

## Auth

Every request: `X-API-Key: <key>` header + request from whitelisted IP.
User-scoped endpoints additionally: `Authorization: Bearer <partner-jwt>`

Partner JWT: issued by POST /token/v1, 15 min TTL, no refresh, opaque (do not parse). Bound to your partner identifier: a token of another partner → 403.
Missing/unknown API key, or missing/invalid/expired JWT → 401 `unauthorized`.
Account state re-checked on every JWT request: blocked or deleted → 403 access_denied, even before the token expires. Check failure → same 403, retryable. Not final: passes again after unblock/restore.

## Error envelope

All errors:
```json
{"error": {"id": "<category>", "msg": "<text>", "ctx": {"code": "<specific-code>"}, "tid": "<trace-id>"}}
```
`ctx` is optional: `ctx.code` is the specific code; some errors add fields (409 idempotency_key_in_flight adds `deal_id`). Categories: `invalid_request` (400/409/422), `unauthorized` (401), `access_denied` (403), `throttling` (429), `internal` (500/502).

## Endpoints

### GET /ping/v1
Auth: X-API-Key
Response 200: `{"status":"ok","partner_id":42}` (affiliate) or `{"status":"ok","partner_ref":"inf_example"}` (influencer, cpa)
Your partner identifier (affiliate ID or ref) is assigned at onboarding; users registered via the API or your referral links are attributed to you by it.

---

### POST /users/v1
Auth: X-API-Key
Register a user. No captcha.

Request:
```json
{"email":"user@example.com","password":"optional","country":"RU"}
```
- `password`: optional; if omitted a random password is set (user signs in via SSO link)
- `country`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, optional, falls back to the default agreed at onboarding

Response 201: `{"user_id":123456}`. Creates a real and a demo account, both USD.

Errors:
- 409 `ctx.code=email_exists` — email already registered
- 403 `ctx.code=country_not_allowed` — country blocked
- 422 `ctx.code=validation` — rejected by the platform
- 400 (no ctx.code) — malformed body / invalid email, details in msg

---

### POST /token/v1
Auth: X-API-Key
Issue partner JWT for a user.

Request: `{"user_id":123456}`

Checks: the user is attributed to you; the account must be active: blocked or deleted → refused; state is read on every call.
On failure: 403 access_denied, no detail (prevents user enumeration).

Response 200:
```json
{"token":"eyJ...","token_type":"Bearer","expires_in":900}
```

---

### POST /users/sso-link/v2
Auth: X-API-Key
Generate one-time SSO URL. Signs the user in on the platform domain serving their country, redirects to redirect_url.

Request:
```json
{"user_id":123456,"redirect_url":"/payin"}
```
- `redirect_url`: relative path only, no `://` — absolute URLs rejected

Response 200:
```json
{"url":"https://<host>/callback/partner-sso/v2/route?token=abc","expires_at":1753700000}
```
URL carries the token only; redirect_url travels inside it.
Link TTL: 3 h. One-time use. One live link per user: a new link cancels the previous one. Messenger link previews do not use it up.
Rate limit: 30/user/hour → 429 on exceed.
Checks: same as /token/v1 → 403; repeated when the link is opened (API access inactive, user not yours, account blocked or deleted → no session, browser redirected to the default page).
When opened, the link refines the user's country from where it is opened and redirects to that country's domain; the session is created there. Do not rely on the host of url.

---

### GET /accounts/v1
Auth: X-API-Key + Bearer JWT
List user's trading accounts.

Response 200:
```json
{"accounts":[{"id":7890001,"type":"real","currency":"USD","balance":1000.00}]}
```
Account types: `real` (real money), `demo` (virtual funds).

---

### POST /ftt/deals/v1
Auth: X-API-Key + Bearer JWT
Open FTT deal. Requires `Idempotency-Key` header (8–128 chars).

Request:
```json
{"account_id":7890001,"amount":10.00,"dir":"up","pair":"EURUSD","group":"real","duration":60}
```
- `dir`: `up` | `down`
- `group`: `real` | `demo`
- `duration`: seconds, must be within pair's min_duration..max_duration

Response 201 (new): `{"deal":{...}}`

Deal object:
```json
{"id":555001,"account_id":7890001,"status":"proceed","pair":"EURUSD","dir":"up","amount":10.00,"group":"real","win_percent":82,"time_open":1753700000,"time_close":1753700060}
```
`account_id`: account the deal was opened on — use it to tell apart deals of two accounts within the same `group`.
Statuses (exact values): `proceed` (open) → `win` | `loose` (lost) | `standoff` (closed at open price) | `cancel` (cancelled by platform) | `error` (platform error, contact support)

Errors:
- 400 `ctx.code=idempotency_key_required` — missing Idempotency-Key or not 8–128 chars
- 409 `ctx.code=idempotency_key_in_flight` — see Idempotency
- 422 `ctx.code=idempotency_key_conflict` — same key, different body
- 422 business errors, `ctx.code` is lowercase text, compare exactly: `insufficiently funds`, `not enough money to trade`, `common not enough real funds`, `insufficient bonus balance`, `amount limit`, `pair amount limit`, `all pairs amount limit`, `pair amount time limit exceed` / `all pairs amount time limit exceed` (+ ` (minute)`/` (hour)`/` (day)` variants), `max deal limit exceed`, `invalid duration`, `pair unavailable`, `pair unavailable on open`, `pair unavailable on close`, `quotes not available`, `account not found`, `location not allowed`, `restricted personally`, `validation`. Others may appear — any 422 means the deal was not opened.

---

### GET /ftt/deals/v1
Auth: X-API-Key + Bearer JWT
Fetch deals by IDs.

Query: `?group=real&ids=555001,555002` (`group` required: `real`|`demo`; `ids` comma-separated, max 100; omit → empty array)

Response 200: `{"deals":[{...}]}`
Deal object: same schema as POST response.

Errors:
- 400 `ctx.code=invalid_group` — group missing or not real/demo
- 400 `ctx.code=too_many_ids` — more than 100 IDs
- 400 `ctx.code=invalid_ids` — non-integer or non-positive ID

---

### GET /ftt/deals/v1/limits
Auth: X-API-Key + Bearer JWT
Deal amount limits per currency.

Response 200:
```json
{"limits":[{"currency":"USD","min":1.00,"default":1.00}]}
```

---

### GET /ftt/pairs/v1
Auth: X-API-Key (no JWT)
Available FTT trading pairs. Disabled/locked pairs excluded.

Response 200:
```json
{"pairs":[{"id":"EURUSD","title":"EUR/USD","group":"forex","precision":5,"min_duration":30,"max_duration":300,"time_close":1790542800,"time_open":1790546400,"win_percent":82},{"id":"BTCUSD","title":"BTC/USD","group":"crypto","precision":2,"min_duration":60,"max_duration":600}]}
```
- `time_close`/`time_open`: the next trading break as Unix timestamps — trading stops at `time_close`, resumes at `time_open` (close comes first, both usually in the future); no break scheduled → both keys absent (BTCUSD above), the pair trades 24/7 — check key presence, not `== 0`
- every listed pair is tradable now until `time_close`; during a break the pair is absent from the list
- `win_percent`: omitted if unavailable

Use `id` as `pair` in deal requests.

## Rate limits

600 req/min per partner (all endpoints), 100 req/min per user (user-scoped endpoints), 30 SSO links/user/hour.
429 `throttling`, `ctx.limit` = limit hit, `ctx.expired` = window reset (Unix seconds, fractional). Retry after it.

## Idempotency (POST /ftt/deals/v1)

Same key + same body within 24h → 409 `idempotency_key_in_flight`, no second deal created.
  error.ctx.deal_id present → deal was opened, poll `GET /ftt/deals/v1?group=...&ids=<deal_id>`.
  error.ctx.deal_id absent → still in progress or ambiguous: retry with the same key shortly; if it persists, contact support — never reopen with a new key.
Same key + different body → 422 `idempotency_key_conflict`.
On 422 business error: deal not opened, retry with same key is safe.
On network error or 5xx/timeout: outcome unknown — retry with the SAME key, never a new one (a new key can open a duplicate deal).
  201 → first attempt never arrived, deal opened now; 409 with deal_id → deal was opened;
  409 without deal_id → still in progress or ambiguous: retry with same key after a few seconds, if it persists contact support.

## Integration sequence

```
POST /users/v1            → user_id
POST /token/v1            → bearer JWT (reissue before 15 min elapse or on 401)
POST /users/sso-link/v2   → one-time URL → redirect user's browser
GET  /ftt/pairs/v1        → pick pair + check min/max duration
GET  /accounts/v1         → get account_id, check balance vs limits
GET  /ftt/deals/v1/limits → validate amount >= min
POST /ftt/deals/v1        → deal_id
GET  /ftt/deals/v1?group=real&ids=   → poll until status != proceed
```

## Full OpenAPI spec

See `swagger.partner.yaml` (next to this file) for complete schema definitions with all field constraints.

---

# Quotes WebSocket

Real-time mid prices of the trading pairs. Endpoint: `wss://partner-ws.1f3d4.tech/`

## Auth

Handshake headers: `X-API-Key: <key>` (same key as the Partner API) + connection from a whitelisted IP. Set your own `User-Agent` (Python's `Python-urllib` default is rejected at the edge). `Origin` is not checked. No user JWT.

Refusals are not HTTP statuses: the handshake completes (101), then the server closes at once with code 1008 and reason `missing_key` | `invalid_key` | `ip_not_allowed` | `inactive` | `connection_limit` (keep under 10 concurrent connections per key). Connection attempts are rate-limited per IP: HTTP 429 before the handshake (may arrive as 502) → back off.

## Frames

Both directions: a JSON array of events, possibly several per frame — process the whole array.
Event: `{"e": <code>, "t": <1 push (default) | 2 request | 3 response>, "uuid": "<your id>", "d": <data>, "err": [{"mess","code"}]}`
Response: same `e` and `uuid`, `t: 3`; failed response has `err` and no `d`. Error codes: `invalid_request` (bad data, unknown or disabled pair; unparseable frame → `e: 0`), `unknown_event`, `system_error` (retry). Connection stays open on errors.

## Events

- 12 subscribe (request): `[{"e":12,"t":2,"uuid":"s1","d":[{"pair":"EURUSD"},{"pair":"GBPUSD"}]}]` → `[{"e":12,"t":3,"uuid":"s1"}]`. Pair IDs = `id` from GET /ftt/pairs/v1. `{"pair":"*"}` = all pairs incl. future ones. One unknown pair fails the whole request, nothing changes. No pair limit; duplicates are not duplicated.
- 13 unsubscribe (request): same shape. Unsubscribing `*` keeps pairs subscribed by name.
- 1 tick (push): `[{"e":1,"d":[{"p":"EURUSD","t":1793633897.821,"q":1.11976}]}]`. `p` pair, `t` Unix seconds with ms (float), `q` mid rounded to pair precision. One tick per event; a frame may carry several tick events — iterate all events and all `d` items. No snapshot: first tick on next price change. Per pair ticks never go back in time.
- 220 closing (push): `[{"e":220,"d":[]}]`, then close 1012 `Reconnect required` in a few seconds → reconnect now and resubscribe.

Subscriptions belong to the connection: resubscribe after every reconnect.

## Flow control

Read continuously. A lagging client gets the latest unsent price per pair (older ones are replaced), but data already in network buffers arrives first. A client that stops reading is dropped without a close frame: after buffers fill, a write over 10 s drops it; with nothing to send, the 60 s ping timeout applies. Server pings every 15 s; the library must answer pings; no answer for ~60 s → closed. Inbound frame max 64 KiB (else close 1009). Many requests without reading responses → close 1008 `too many pending responses`.

## Close codes

- 1008 `missing_key` | `invalid_key` | `ip_not_allowed` | `inactive` | `connection_limit` — refused at connect.
- 1008 `card changed: <reason>` — access revoked while connected (key revoked, suspended, IP removed); fix the setup, do not loop.
- 1008 `too many pending responses`; 1009 frame too big; 1012 `Reconnect required` — planned restart.
- No close frame — network drop or stalled reader.

Reconnect: on 220/1012 at once; otherwise exponential backoff 1 s → 60 s cap with jitter; never retry `invalid_key`/`ip_not_allowed`/`inactive` in a loop.
